exercise.name: Dumbbell Lateral Lunge with Cross Body Row

reference.title: Dumbbell Lateral Lunge with Cross Body Row
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked from this environment); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip, knee and ankle; shoulder and elbow)
exercise.laterality: Unilateral (lunge right, row with the left arm)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as you step out and sit back; breathe out as you row; breathe in as you lower the dumbbell; breathe out as you push back to the middle.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s down, 0.8 s row, 1.2 s lower, 0.9 s up

prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbell, or two rows per lunge. Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.

cues.text: Stand tall, feet hip width, a dumbbell in the left hand at the side.
Take a wide step straight out to the right, toes forward or slightly out; land softly.
Sit the hips back over the right foot, left leg straight, both heels down; hinge forward with a flat back and let the dumbbell reach down and across toward the inside of the right knee.
Hold the lunge and row the dumbbell diagonally up across your body to the left side of your waist; elbow back, shoulder blade squeezed; breathe out.
Lower the dumbbell back across under control, then drive through the right heel back to the middle and step the feet together.
Stand tall and repeat; switch sides (the player mirrors).

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back to reach across
mistakes.fix: Hinge from the hips with a flat back; reach only as far as you can keep it flat.

mistakes.mistake: Twisting the trunk to lift the dumbbell
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest square to the floor; the arm does the row.
Keep the right knee over the toes.
Drive the elbow back toward the hip and keep the shoulder away from the ear.

kinematics.peak: 79 cm between ankle centres (about one leg length)
kinematics.norm: Wide lateral step, about one leg length; Riemann 2013 tested lateral steps of up to 60% of body height
About 80-90 degrees at the bottom (clinical opinion); patellofemoral stress rises with knee flexion in side lunges (Escamilla 2008)

kinematics.peak: ≈34° forward, flat back, held still through the row
kinematics.norm: Hinged forward with a neutral spine for the reach and row (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Reach: left hand -2.3 cm right of the pelvis midline, 44.6 cm above the floor, elbow ≈2°
kinematics.peak: Top: hand -32.8 cm (left of the midline) beside the waist, elbow ≈119° and -0.7 cm relative to the shoulder joint height
kinematics.norm: Diagonal path from the inside of the stepping knee to the opposite side of the waist (common coaching)

kinematics.peak: Step out 0.6 s, 1.2 s down, row 0.8 s up, 0.3 s squeeze, 1.2 s down, 0.85 s up, step in 0.65 s
kinematics.norm: Controlled; pause briefly at the top of the row (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #25833, Dumbbell Lateral Lunge with Cross Body Row, video (movement reference)
Riemann et al. 2013, biomechanical comparison of forward and lateral lunges at varying step lengths (J Sports Med Phys Fitness 53:130-138)
Escamilla et al. 2008, patellofemoral compressive force and stress during forward and side lunges with and without a stride (Clin Biomech 23:1026-1037)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Clear the floor to the side before stepping out.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee or groin discomfort: a shorter step and a shallower lunge.
Back discomfort: less hinge and a shorter reach.
regressions: Lateral lunge and the row done separately (one-arm row with a bench).
progressions: Add a pause at the top of each row.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Stepping-leg knee extensor: lowers and drives the push back to the middle (Riemann 2013 on lateral lunges).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Stepping-leg hip extensor as the hips sit back and drive up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: The straight leg's adductors lengthen as the hips shift right and help pull the body back to the middle (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Assist hip extension of the bent leg out of the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension with the trunk hinged forward (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the stepping knee tracking over the toes (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Hold the straight leg long (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the stepping foot with the heel down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull the upper arm back and down in the row (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Squeeze the shoulder blade back at the top of the row (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Draws the arm back past the trunk, especially as the dumbbell crosses toward the hip (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Bend the elbow as the dumbbell rises (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulder up against the hanging dumbbell (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Braces the hinged trunk against the one-sided pull of the row (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the trunk turning toward the rowing arm (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Work with the right obliques to keep the trunk square (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the back flat in the forward hinge (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the back flat in the forward hinge (clinical opinion).

phases.label: Stand tall, dumbbell in the left hand
Lower, push back to the middle

guides.label: Hips sit back over the foot
Row diagonally across to the hip
